title: Quantum Tensor Network Learning with DMRG
authors: Gustav J L Jäger, Martin B Plenio, Hans-Martin Rieser
abstract: Tensor Networks are a relatively new machine learning approach. The architectures proposed initially are inspired by approaches from quantum many-body physics simulations. One common layout is the matrix product state (MPS) also known as a tensor train optimized with gradient descent techniques. We introduce a global normalization condition, so that the MPS represents a quantum state. We investigate two optimization methods that find the locally optimal tensors and compare them regarding their effectiveness. One is based on gradient descent and the other on an adaptation of DMRG.
summary: This paper adapts Tensor Network methods, specifically using the MPS ansatz, for machine learning tasks by enforcing a global quantum normalization constraint. It compares gradient descent and a modified DMRG approach for optimizing the network parameters. The work shows that these quantum-inspired optimization techniques can achieve high accuracy on classical datasets, advancing the field of quantum machine learning.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of adapting Tensor Network (TN) methods, originally from quantum many-body physics, for use in classical machine learning by enforcing a global normalization condition.
main_result: The modified DMRG approach achieves performance comparable to gradient descent methods, demonstrating that incorporating the normalization constraint significantly improves both the loss and accuracy of the learning process.
method: The authors compare two optimization techniques—gradient descent and an adaptation of DMRG—for optimizing the parameters of a Matrix Product State (MPS) ansatz.
model_or_system: The core model is an MPS ansatz used to represent a quantum state, which is then optimized using ML loss functions derived from data (e.g., MNIST dataset).
key_observables: Loss function (L), training/testing accuracy, and the norm of the MPS.
important_parameters: The step size $\alpha$ in gradient descent, and the bond dimension used in the MPS representation.
main_assumptions: The DMRG adaptation requires a post-processing step because the standard algorithm does not naturally incorporate the full ML loss function gradient term.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the MPS architecture; Figure 2 compares the loss convergence over iterative steps for different optimization methods; Table 1 provides a quantitative comparison of accuracy and loss.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the mathematical formulation of the loss function and the two optimization methods (gradient descent and DMRG adaptation), presents quantitative comparisons in a table, and discusses the results and limitations.
why_interesting: It bridges the gap between advanced quantum simulation techniques (DMRG, TNs) and modern machine learning optimization, providing a concrete framework for quantum machine learning.
